title: Exchange compatibility for a strict-local representative map
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, f:X→Y a scheme morphism, s:Spec Ω→Y a geometric point with Ω algebraically closed, and (g′:X′→X,f′:X′→Spec Ω,f,s) a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let F be a Λ-module sheaf on X_et. Put R=O^sh_(Y,s), ρ:Spec R→Y, Z=X×_Y Spec R and p:Z→X as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit; def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], H=p⁻¹F. Suppose t:Spec Ω→Spec R restricts along every affine pointed-neighbourhood limit leg c_V to its specified point v. Suppose q:X′→Z satisfies qh=f′t and qp=g′, where h:Z→Spec R. Let a:(f_*F)_s→Γ(Z,H) be ANY module morphism satisfying IsQcqsStrictLocalModuleComparison [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-strict-local-module-comparison], namely germ_(V,v) followed by a is the unit/limit-leg restriction r_V for every affine pointed representative. Then the identity geometric stalk of baseChangeMap [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] equals upperStarCompSheafFiberIso(s,id).hom, the equality transport from the stalk at id≫s to that at s, a, globalSectionsUpperStarMap(q,H), the global-section map of upperStarComp(q,p,g′,hq.symm).inv, lowerStarCompGlobalSectionsIso(f′).inv, the global-to-terminal-section identification on Spec Ω, and its identity-neighbourhood germ, in this order. No qcqs or properness assumption, no local-ring or closed-point structure, and no invertibility of a is required. Stalks and germs are the actual site-point fibre functors [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]; restriction on global sections is [def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback].

proof.text: Cancel the canonical inverse-image stalk isomorphism. Initiality of the small affine pointed representative functor identifies its germ cocone as a colimit, so apply colimit hom-ext. On each representative use exchange_pointed_representative; substitute strictLocal_section_pullback, and then the assumed comparison germ formula ha. Associativity gives the claimed equality.
